report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
Under the EU AI Act as originally adopted in 2024, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were due to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence). However, the AI Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, amended Article 113 to push this application date back to 2 December 2027 (high confidence). Related deadlines—2 August 2028 for Annex I product-embedded high-risk systems, and 2 August 2026/2 December 2026 for transparency obligations under Article 50—remain relevant but distinct from the Annex III timeline.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (2024 Text)
Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, Article 113 set 2 August 2026 (36 months after entry into force) as the date from which high-risk AI system obligations, including those for Annex III systems, would apply (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [EU AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). The Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with Chapters I and II applying from 2 February 2025, and certain governance provisions (Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII, Chapter XII, Article 78) applying from 2 August 2025, except Article 101 (medium confidence) ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### Revised Timeline Under the AI Omnibus
The AI Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) amended Article 113, extending the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [European Commission Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). As amended, Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (excluding Article 6(5)) are now stated to apply from 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems (medium confidence) ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). The Omnibus separately extended the application date for high-risk AI systems embedded in products covered by EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I) to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [European Commission Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

### Legislative Process and Entry Into Force
The Commission had proposed adjusting the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, conditional on confirmation that necessary standards and tools were available; Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this Omnibus on 7 May 2026 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The Omnibus was reportedly adopted on 19 November 2025, with political agreement on 7 May 2026 and entry into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Related and Adjacent Deadlines
Transparency obligations under Article 50 apply from 2 August 2026, with a transitional period until 2 December 2026 for marking/detection duties under Article 50(2) for systems already on the market (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [euaicompass.com](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). New prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM-generating systems apply from 2 December 2026, alongside transitional compliance deadlines for certain providers already on the market before 2 August 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). Operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before the applicable Chapter III date are subject to the Regulation only if the systems undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A clear contradiction exists between pre-Omnibus sources (reflecting the original 2024 text) that cite 2 August 2026 as the Annex III deadline, and post-Omnibus sources that cite 2 December 2027 ([CSA Lab Space](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) vs. [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). This reflects a timing issue: several sources were apparently written before the Omnibus entered into force (27 July 2026) and have not been updated. A low-confidence claim (0.12) regarding specific Annex III provider obligations under Articles 8–15 comes from a single, non-authoritative source and should be treated with caution ([Annex III obligations guide](https://ai-act-readiness.example/annex-iii-obligations-guide)). Similarly, a low-confidence claim (0.17) describing 2 August 2026 as still "live" as of April 2026 likely predates the Omnibus's entry into force.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the Commission retained conditionality—delaying the deadline further pending confirmation that standards/tools are ready—or whether 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 are fixed backstop dates. The full consolidated text of amended Article 113 is not reproduced in available sources, leaving ambiguity about which specific Annex III sub-provisions apply on which date. The interaction between the "significant design change" transitional rule (Article 111(2)) and the new 2027 date is unaddressed. Further research into the official consolidated EUR-Lex text and Commission implementation guidance is needed to resolve these gaps.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
Under the EU AI Act as originally adopted in 2024, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were due to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence). However, the AI Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, amended Article 113 to push this application date back to 2 December 2027 (high confidence). Related deadlines—2 August 2028 for Annex I product-embedded high-risk systems, and 2 August 2026/2 December 2026 for transparency obligations under Article 50—remain relevant but distinct from the Annex III timeline.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (2024 Text)
Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, Article 113 set 2 August 2026 (36 months after entry into force) as the date from which high-risk AI system obligations, including those for Annex III systems, would apply (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [EU AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). The Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with Chapters I and II applying from 2 February 2025, and certain governance provisions (Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII, Chapter XII, Article 78) applying from 2 August 2025, except Article 101 (medium confidence) ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### Revised Timeline Under the AI Omnibus
The AI Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) amended Article 113, extending the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [European Commission Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). As amended, Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (excluding Article 6(5)) are now stated to apply from 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems (medium confidence) ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). The Omnibus separately extended the application date for high-risk AI systems embedded in products covered by EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I) to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [European Commission Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

### Legislative Process and Entry Into Force
The Commission had proposed adjusting the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, conditional on confirmation that necessary standards and tools were available; Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this Omnibus on 7 May 2026 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The Omnibus was reportedly adopted on 19 November 2025, with political agreement on 7 May 2026 and entry into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Related and Adjacent Deadlines
Transparency obligations under Article 50 apply from 2 August 2026, with a transitional period until 2 December 2026 for marking/detection duties under Article 50(2) for systems already on the market (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [euaicompass.com](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). New prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM-generating systems apply from 2 December 2026, alongside transitional compliance deadlines for certain providers already on the market before 2 August 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). Operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before the applicable Chapter III date are subject to the Regulation only if the systems undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A clear contradiction exists between pre-Omnibus sources (reflecting the original 2024 text) that cite 2 August 2026 as the Annex III deadline, and post-Omnibus sources that cite 2 December 2027 ([CSA Lab Space](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) vs. [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). This reflects a timing issue: several sources were apparently written before the Omnibus entered into force (27 July 2026) and have not been updated. A low-confidence claim (0.12) regarding specific Annex III provider obligations under Articles 8–15 comes from a single, non-authoritative source and should be treated with caution ([Annex III obligations guide](https://ai-act-readiness.example/annex-iii-obligations-guide)). Similarly, a low-confidence claim (0.17) describing 2 August 2026 as still "live" as of April 2026 likely predates the Omnibus's entry into force.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the Commission retained conditionality—delaying the deadline further pending confirmation that standards/tools are ready—or whether 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 are fixed backstop dates. The full consolidated text of amended Article 113 is not reproduced in available sources, leaving ambiguity about which specific Annex III sub-provisions apply on which date. The interaction between the "significant design change" transitional rule (Article 111(2)) and the new 2027 date is unaddressed. Further research into the official consolidated EUR-Lex text and Commission implementation guidance is needed to resolve these gaps.
